scene: Inferno XXI — boiling pitch conceals barrators; Malebranche hook those who surface
story: Dante and Virgil reach the fifth bolgia, where dark boiling pitch fills a ditch like a shipyard's cauldrons; bubbles rise without revealing all the souls concealed underneath.
A black demon comes racing over the bridge with a corrupt official from Lucca, throws him into the pitch, and hurries away.
The Malebranche demons threaten anyone who lifts their back above the pitch; their hooks force emerging souls back under its surface.
Virgil hides Dante and approaches the demons to negotiate passage, confronting Malacoda, their leader.
Malacoda promises the travelers a way forward and assigns an escort. The truth of his directions remains unverified here and is tested in later cantos.
Dante emerges from hiding and follows Virgil, apprehensive of the demons' threatening behavior. Their dangerous escort continues into Canto XXII.

Surface event reveals an occupant at one time, not uninterrupted visibility
Threatened exposure and forced re-submergence must retain their causal order
A demon's promised route is testimony, not verified safety
